July 2026 NETGEAR Security Advisory
3
                                        people found this helpful in last 30 days
NETGEAR's Product Security Team has assessed the following product vulnerabilities and provided guidance to address these vulnerabilities in the table below.
Because firmware updates contain security fixes, bug fixes, and new features for your products, we strongly advise you to enable automatic firmware updates on supported devices. For older products, we advise you to download and install new firmware updates as soon as possible or follow the guidance provided for devices that require other remediation steps.
CVE-2026-15757 Insufficient input validation vulnerability in NETGEAR DGND3700v1 modem router
A security flaw was discovered in the NETGEAR DGND3700v1 that could allow someone on the same local WiFi network to send unauthorized commands to the device.
This issue was identified through testing in a controlled research environment using a simulated version of the router's software and has not been confirmed on physical production devices.
Severity:
MEDIUM
Acknowledgments: Security Research Center (SRC) @ Concordia University
Affected Products
DGND3700v1
Recommendation
NETGEAR DGND3700v1 has reached End-of-Support phase, and no further security updates are planned. NETGEAR strongly recommends replacing these devices with newer NETGEAR models to ensure continued security support and updates.
CVE-2026-62655 A DoS vulnerability due to stack overflow exists in certain NETGEAR Orbi models
A security flaw was found in certain NETGEAR Orbi models that could allow an unauthorized user to cause the device to stop responding or restart unexpectedly, disrupting network connectivity and making the device temporarily unavailable.
Severity:
MEDIUM
Acknowledgments: fxc233

CVE-2026-62656 Post-authenticated command injection vulnerability found in certain NETGEAR RAX models
A security flaw was found in certain NETGEAR RAX models that could allow a logged-in user to send specially crafted requests to the router and run unauthorized commands. This could enable the user to make unauthorized changes to the router and affect its security and operation.

MEDIUM
